newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World airline clearing system hit record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: World airline clearing system hit record in 1996.

text.p: The world airline body IATA's clearing house, which settles billing between companies in the industry, processed a record $27.9 billion in 1996, the organisation reported on Friday.

This meant that just over one quarter of the industry's turnover for scheduled international flights -- which hit $130 billion in 1995 -- was passing through the system which settles most debts without cash transfers.

The clearing house, which completed its 50th year of operations last year, sets off against each other claims from airlines for passengers and cargo carried for, and services provided to, other companies, through a netting process.

IATA, the 254-member International Air Transport Association, said passenger business which went through the system last year increased 9.5 per cent over 1995 to a total of $17.2 billion - just over 61 per cent of the total cleared.
Cargo interline business grew 3.2 per cent to $1.06 billion, or 3.8 per cent of the total.

Clearance of billing for services -- which include engineering and maintenance, aircraft leasing, reservation services, passenger handling, catering and communications -- rose 7.3 per cent to $8.2 billion, or 29.3 per cent.
Airline credit card ticketing, IATA said, remained static at just under $1.6 billion -- 5.7 per cent of the clearing house total.

Clearing house membership in 1996 totalled a record 269 -- which included 195 IATA airlines and 74 non-IATA carriers as well as airline-owned companies, sponsored airlines and special accounts, IATA said.
The clearing house, which employs 11 staff, is based in Geneva.
